title: GPU heatband cluster/pool weekly coverage (Jul 14-20 2026)
content:
Purpose: weekly 'heatband' style export that shows how much of the GPU fleet sits in utilization bands throughout the day (0-10, 10-50, 50-80, 80-100%). Intent is to give a quick signal for fragmentation, headroom, and sustained congestion across clusters and pools so infra and SRE can prioritize reservations, burst policies and reclaim/backfill windows.

Methodology:
- Source: production telemetry pipeline (ingest-prod.gpu_telemetry) aggregated to per-cluster, per-pool, hourly percent utilization.
- Bands computed on per-hour basis: low (0-10%), light (10-50%), medium (50-80%), high (80-100%).
- Weekly coverage = percent of hours in the week each cluster/pool spent in that band.
- This sheet groups clusters by region and flags sustained high-band runs (>12 hours in high band per day average).

How to read the heatband rows: each row is a cluster or pool. Columns show percent-hours in band during the week. Higher % in high-band = sustained congestion; high % in low-band = fragmentation/idle headroom.

Top-line summary (Jul 14-20):
- Fleet average: low 28%, light 42%, medium 18%, high 12%
- APAC-1 clusters show elevated high-band: APAC-1-a (high 29%), APAC-1-b (high 25%)
- EU clusters relatively light; EMEA-pool-3 has high medium-band (35%) indicating increased mid-range load that benefits from smaller reservations
- NA: several bursty clusters (NA-gamma, NA-delta) with 40%+ in light band but low high-band, suggesting opportunities for burst credits instead of reservations

ASCII sample table (percent-hours in band, week):
Cluster/Pool            | low(0-10) | light(10-50) | medium(50-80) | high(80-100)
------------------------|-----------|--------------|---------------|------------
APAC-1-a (gpu-c7)       | 12%       | 34%          | 25%           | 29%
APAC-1-b (gpu-c8)       | 18%       | 32%          | 25%           | 25%
NA-gamma (shared-v2)    | 45%       | 42%          | 9%            | 4%
EMEA-pool-3 (res-v1)    | 22%       | 18%          | 35%           | 25%
NA-delta (burstable)    | 50%       | 40%          | 8%            | 2%

Anomalies flagged this week:
- APAC-1-a: two sustained high-band windows coincident with model tuning jobs (2026-07-16 03:00-12:00 UTC). Tagged JIRA-OPS-4281.
- EMEA-pool-3: medium-band drift without matching user requests spike — likely scheduled training backlog (check team: solutions-modeling).
- NA-gamma: high fragmentation (45% low) despite increased overall calls; investigate packing inefficiency and small-job placement.

Suggested actions (prioritized):
1) Short-term (1-3 days):
   - Move some low-priority training to NA-delta burstable pool from APAC-1-a for the 07/16-07/18 window (contact: Lina).
   - Temporarily raise burst capacity on APAC-1 clusters during predicted night tuning windows.
2) Medium-term (2-4 weeks):
   - Introduce tighter bin-packing advice for small jobs in NA-gamma (scheduler change: prefer colocations, 2 jobs per GPU slot for <2k token workloads).
   - Add a reservation slot for EMEA-pool-3 of 4 GPUs for evening training windows to reduce medium-band drift.
3) Long-term: revisit autoscaler signals to include heatband percent-hours as a trigger for proactive scale-up rather than pure instantaneous utilization.

Queries & dashboards used:
- heatband aggregation: bq query 'select cluster, pool, band, count_hour from redwood_prod.analytics.weekly_heatbands where week_start='2026-07-14''
- grafana panel: GPU > Heatband Coverage (dashboard id: heatband)
- placement logs: gs://redwood-telemetry/placement/2026/07/14-20/*

Open questions / notes to reviewer:
- Are the sustained APAC tuning jobs organic or ad-hoc (ask solutions-modeling)?
- Should we set a temporary hard cap for non-prod training in APAC-1 during business hours?

Appendix (quick diff vs prior week):
- Fleet high-band increased +3 percentage points week-over-week (was 9% -> now 12%).
- APAC high-band increased +8pp. NA fragmentation increased slightly (+2pp low-band).

Prepared by: Aisha Patel (eng-infrastructure)
Quick contacts: Diego (infra telemetry), Lina (scheduling), Omar (regional ops)
